Estimate a correlation network

Source: R/correlation.R
cor_network.Rd

cor_network() estimates a correlation network, in which each pair of variables is joined by their marginal (zero-order) correlation. An edge shows that two variables covary without controlling for any other variable, so it also reflects associations that run through other variables in the network.

The correlations are computed from raw data, or taken from a supplied correlation matrix. cor_method chooses Pearson, Spearman, Kendall or polychoric and polyserial correlations; alpha keeps only correlations that differ significantly from zero, with an optional multiple-comparison adjustment (adjust); threshold removes weak correlations.

cor_network() returns the correlation matrix as a network; the network involves no optimization and has no certificate.

The network gives a descriptive overview of the association structure, such as the clustering of items or symptoms, but it does not separate direct from indirect associations. For associations that control for the other variables use pcor_network() (all partial correlations) or ebic_glasso() (a regularized partial-correlation network); tmfg_network() filters the correlations to a sparse backbone. The network is the "cor" estimator of bootnet.

Usage

cor_network(
  data = NULL,
  cor_matrix = NULL,
  n = NULL,
  cor_method = c("pearson", "spearman", "kendall", "auto"),
  threshold = 0,
  alpha = NULL,
  adjust = "none",
  na_method = c("pairwise", "listwise"),
  labels = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A numeric data frame or matrix with one row per observation. Not needed when cor_matrix is given. Ordered factors enter as their level codes; other non-numeric columns are dropped with a message, and constant or all-missing columns with a warning.

cor_matrix

A correlation matrix to use instead of data; a covariance matrix is rescaled to a correlation matrix. With alpha, n is then required.

n

Sample size of cor_matrix, needed only for the significance test: a single number >= 1, and a whole number >= 3 when alpha is set. Ignored when data is given.

cor_method

Correlation computed from data: "pearson" (default), "spearman", "kendall", or "auto" (polychoric and polyserial correlations for ordinal items; see cor_auto()).

threshold

Absolute edge weight below which an edge is set to zero: a single number >= 0. Default 0. A logical value (the threshold = TRUE rule of qgraph) is refused; use alpha for a significance rule.

alpha

Significance level in (0, 1): edges not significant at this level are set to zero. Default NULL, no test. A Kendall test needs raw data; partial Kendall correlations cannot be tested.

adjust

Multiple-comparison adjustment of the edge p-values, any method of stats::p.adjust(). Default "none".

na_method

Handling of missing values in data: "pairwise" (default) uses pairwise-complete correlations adjusted to the nearest positive-definite matrix; "listwise" drops incomplete rows. The two agree for complete data.

labels

Optional node labels, one unique label per node of the network.

Value

A fitted network of class psychnet (psychnet) whose edge weights are correlations. as.data.frame() returns one row per edge with columns from, to and weight; certificate() reports that the network has no certificate. The object also stores the correlation matrix (cor_matrix), the sample size (n_eff; with pairwise data, the median number of observations per pair), the missing-data handling used (na_method; "none" with cor_matrix), the observations per pair when estimated from data (n_pair) and, with alpha, the unadjusted p-values (p_values). Nodes keep the column order of the input.

Details

Each correlation is tested against zero with the statistic \(t = r \sqrt{df / (1 - r^2)}\) on \(df = n - 2\) degrees of freedom for a correlation and \(df = n - p\) for a full-order partial correlation of \(p\) variables. With na_method = "pairwise" and incomplete data, a correlation is tested with the number of observations available for that pair. Kendall correlations use a tie-corrected asymptotic test of the raw data. The p-values are adjusted over the distinct pairs and are computed from the correlations before threshold is applied; an edge is kept only if it passes both rules.

Conditions

psychnet_degenerate_sample (error, also of class psychnet_bad_input) when the sample is too small for the test (\(df \le 0\)); psychnet_bad_input when an argument is out of range, threshold is logical, cor_matrix is not a finite, symmetric, positive semi-definite matrix with a positive diagonal, n is missing with cor_matrix and alpha, a Kendall test is requested with cor_matrix, data has fewer than two usable variables, a pair of variables is never observed together, or labels do not match the nodes; psychnet_constant_variable (warning) when a constant or all-missing column is dropped. A psychnet_dropped_columns message names non-numeric columns that were dropped.

See also

pcor_network(); ebic_glasso(); tmfg_network(); psychnet(), which routes method = "cor" here; psychnet for the result.

Examples

x <- matrix(stats::rnorm(200 * 4), 200, 4)
cor_network(x)
#> <psychnet> cor network
#>   nodes: 4   edges: 6   (undirected)
cor_network(x, alpha = 0.05, adjust = "BH")
#> <psychnet> cor network
#>   nodes: 4   edges: 0   (undirected)
